findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the back-out/compensating-forward procedure: on any post-verification MISSING>0 (or per-issue completeness failure), the exact steps to re-post the affected distinct body from backup/<KEY>.json, and note that original id/created/author cannot be reproduced (DATA LOSS RISK) so the restore is a best-effort re-post.
evidence: Comment DELETE is a one-way transformation with no native undo (T11 POST-ROLLBACK-STATE applicability (d)); the plan attests backups exist and MISSING=0 held, but no criterion states the remediation if MISSING>0 were found.
The plan asserts backup completeness and post-verification but is silent on the recovery action (re-post from backup) that makes the backup a genuine back-out path.
DATA LOSS RISK: a verification that discovers a fully-deleted distinct body has no described repair; original comment id/created/author cannot be recreated identically via the create-comment API.
findings.finding: The plan guarantees a completeness-checked pre-deletion backup and post-deletion MISSING=0 verification, but never specifies the BACK-OUT / compensating-forward procedure to be taken if verification detects a missing distinct body — i.e., how a backed-up comment would be re-posted after an irreversible DELETE. A backup is only a rollback path if paired with a restore action.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria — 'Pre-deletion backup' and 'Post-deletion re-fetch shows zero missing distinct bodies ... confirmed independently against the backups (MISSING=0 on all 27)'
scenarios: A body-normalization or ambiguity edge causes every copy of a distinct body to be deleted on one issue; post-verification flags MISSING>0 but no procedure exists to restore it.
REB-1861 (largest, run last) fails post-verification after deletions have landed; operator needs a defined restore-from-backup step under time pressure.

evidence: 1 criterion line(s) bundle multiple deliverables with 'and' (split so each is independently verifiable).
findings.suggested_fix: Split compound criteria, replace subjective terms with observable outcomes, and state how each is verified.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the Jira Cloud auth/HTTPS precondition for the DELETE run — the specific project permission the bot principal must hold (e.g. 'Delete all comments', not merely 'own') and the HTTPS/credential basis — and specify handling for HTTP 403 distinct from the idempotent-success 404.
evidence: Plan quotes only 429/Retry-After and '5xx/transient' handling plus 'A 404 on DELETE is idempotent success' — no 403/permission path is named
ABSENCE: no statement of the Jira 'Delete all comments' project permission required for the bot principal to delete comments, nor the HTTPS/credential precondition
T3(c): auth/HTTPS preconditions must be stated for an external API integration; deleting comments across 27 issues can require the broader 'all' (not 'own') delete-comment permission
Prior plan-review cache for this ticket independently raised the same auth-precondition gap (.rebar/cache/plan-review/76b2-4b5f-5682-45e5/8010072... and d14503...)
findings.finding: The plan depends on ~30k authenticated Jira Cloud DELETE calls but states no auth/permission precondition (T3 check c): it does not name the Jira project permission the bot principal must hold to delete these comments ('Delete all comments' vs merely 'Delete own comments'), nor the HTTPS/credential basis, and it does not distinguish an HTTP 403 permission-denied from the 404 it treats as idempotent success.
findings.location: Full plan narrative comment — 'Rate limiting — 429 IS retried' bullet and the '404 on DELETE is idempotent success' clause; AC 'Every DELETE honoured Retry-After on 429'
scenarios: The bot principal holds 'Delete own comments' but not 'Delete all comments'; every DELETE returns 403 and the run, whose only permission-aware branch is 429/Retry-After + 404-as-success, either aborts or mis-classifies the 403
A 403 is silently counted like a 404 'already gone', leaving duplicates in place while the log reports success
findings.suggested_fix: Add a precondition line naming the required Jira permission and confirming it holds for accountId 712020:6471376f-…, plus a rule that any 403 aborts the affected issue for manual review (never counted as an idempotent 404).

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Define the exact normalization applied to comment bodies for the distinct-body dedup key, and add an over-merge guard that is independent of that normalization (e.g. verify against the raw backed-up bodies / count of pre-run distinct RAW bodies), so an over-merging normalization cannot pass its own post-verification.
evidence: 'the kept id per body, and the delete count'
'assert every distinct normalized body present before the run still has exactly one surviving copy'
ABSENCE: no definition of the normalization applied to comment bodies (e.g. whitespace/ADF/whitespace-marker stripping) anywhere in the plan text
The verification uses the SAME normalization it is validating, so it cannot detect an over-merge produced by that normalization
findings.finding: The dedup identity function is 'distinct NORMALIZED body' but the normalization rule is never defined, and it is load-bearing for an irreversible DELETE; because the per-issue post-verification asserts survival of 'every distinct normalized body' using that same normalization, an over-merging normalization (two genuinely-different comments collapsing to one normalized string) would be silently self-consistent and pass verification while wrongly deleting a distinct comment.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria: dry-run bullet ('distinct-body count, the kept id per body') and post-verification bullet ('every distinct normalized body present before the run still has exactly one surviving copy')
scenarios: Two distinct marked comments whose bodies differ only in content that the normalization discards (e.g. an embedded timestamp, an id marker, or ADF-vs-text differences) collapse to one normalized key; one is deleted and the loss passes post-verification as 'exactly one surviving copy'
findings.suggested_fix: Specify the normalization (fields included, ADF handling, marker/whitespace stripping) and add a cross-check that the number of distinct RAW (un-normalized) marked bodies kept equals the number of survivors, treating any body that normalizes-equal-but-differs-raw as an AMBIGUOUS case to be skipped and reported rather than collapsed.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State, in the plan text, the positive rationale for using distinct-normalized-body as the dedup identity (why it correctly captures the re-posted duplicates and why a marker/source-event id key was not used), so the identity choice is justified rather than deferred to ticket comments.
evidence: 'The full plan narrative, method, and safety rationale are preserved verbatim in this ticket's comments'
'its PRIMARY id-identity dedup skip was inert (comment_ids empty)' — the defect is described in terms of an ID identity, yet the cleanup keys on BODY, without stating why
ABSENCE: no sentence in the plan explaining why body-normalized dedup correctly identifies the re-posted duplicates rather than a proxy that could over- or under-match
findings.finding: The plan does not state a positive rationale in the reviewable text for WHY collapsing by distinct comment body is the correct identity for this defect rather than a proxy — e.g. why body-equality is preferred over keying on the bridge marker's source-event/comment id that the id-dedup was supposed to use. The method/rationale is deferred to ticket comments, so the plan as written asserts the mechanism without justifying the identity choice.
findings.location: Problem section and Acceptance Criteria (dedup by 'distinct-body count' / 'kept id per body')
scenarios: A reviewer/implementer cannot judge whether body-dedup faithfully targets the re-post loop (vs. collapsing legitimate repeated-text comments) because the identity choice is unjustified in the plan text

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add one line reconciling the 30 affected issues vs 27 with deletions (e.g. '3 issues had no true duplicates / were skipped as ambiguous per AC5, hence 0 backups/deletions').
evidence: AC7: 'the run covered exactly it (30 issues)'
AC2: 'backup/<KEY>.json for all 27 issues with deletions'
AC12: 'MISSING=0 on all 27' — the 3-issue gap (30 minus 27) is inferrable from AC5's skip rule but never explicitly stated
findings.finding: The affected-issue count (30) and the deletion/backup count (27) are stated across different ACs without an explicit reconciliation of the 3-issue difference.
findings.location: AC7 ('30 issues') vs AC2 & AC12 ('all 27 issues with deletions', 'MISSING=0 on all 27')
scenarios: A reviewer or auditor cross-checking counts sees 30 vs 27 and cannot tell from the body whether 3 issues were correctly no-op/skipped or silently dropped
findings.suggested_fix: State explicitly that 30 issues were in scope and 27 required deletions; the remaining 3 had no duplicate bodies (or were skipped as ambiguous) and correctly produced no backup or DELETE.
